title: A small covering subfamily of an open sheaf coproduct with an atlas
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. On its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification], let F and F_i (i in an arbitrary Type w) be Type-u-valued sheaves, and let H with injections j_i be their given categorical coproduct [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let q:H to F be epimorphic and let iota_i=j_i q be monomorphisms representable by open immersions [def-pc-subfunctor, def-weil-open-immersion, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose H is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], but impose no diagonal or atlas hypothesis on the F_i. Then there are a type J in Type u and k:J to I such that H with the retained injections j_(k r) is still a coproduct, and every section of F over every scheme T has a u-small fppf covering on each member of which it lifts to one of the retained F_(k r). The label may vary with the covering member; empty schemes and empty index types are allowed.

proof.text: Choose an etale surjective scheme atlas a:h_U to H using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. This is an epimorphism of sheaves: for any scheme test h_T to H, its representable surjective etale pullback W to T is a singleton fppf cover, and the two sheaf maps being compared agree locally after this lift, hence agree by separatedness [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let K be the indices i such that F_i has a section over some nonempty scheme. If i is not in K, F_i has no sections on nonempty schemes and exactly one on empty schemes by the empty-cover axiom. There is a unique natural map from F_i to every sheaf, so F_i is initial.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

proof.text: Let B be the sheaf of continuous maps to the discrete two-point space, supplied by [lem-sfb-set-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf], restricted to the fppf site over S. For every i in K, assign the constant-one map F_i to B and the constant-zero map on every other summand. The coproduct universal property produces chi_i:H to B. If chi_i and chi_j agree after the atlas, they agree on H by Step 1. Evaluation on a section of F_i over a nonempty scheme distinguishes one and zero when i differs from j. Thus i maps injectively to chi_i composed with a in Hom(h_U,B). Yoneda identifies this set with C(|U|,{0,1}), which is u-small. Choose an equivalence of K with J:Type u and let k:J to I be its inclusion. Each omitted summand is initial, so extending a family of maps on the retained summands by the unique maps on initial summands proves that the retained injections into H are still a colimit. This argument precedes every use of a small-index partition theorem and does not require preservation of large coproducts by coefficient lifts.

proof.text: For a section t of F over T let V_i(t) be the open representing h_T times_F F_i. Its open subset is uniquely determined by the pullback property, so inverse image along g:W to T gives V_i(g*t)=g^{-1}V_i(t). Define V(t) as the union of V_(k r)(t) over r in J. Inverse image commutes with unions, so the characteristic maps of these opens give a natural morphism chi:F to O, where O(T) is the sheaf of continuous maps |T| to the Sierpinski space. It is an fppf sheaf by [lem-sfb-set-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf]. On F_(k r) its own pullback open is all of T, since the map lifts through itself. Therefore chi equals the constant full-open map on every retained summand. Their colimit property gives equality after q; Epi q gives equality on F. Thus V(t)=T for every test section.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

proof.text: For each point x of T, choose r with x in V_(k r)(t). The corresponding open neighbourhoods, indexed by the u-small underlying set of T, cover T. They are a Zariski cover, hence an fppf cover by [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. The universal section of each represented pullback gives the required section in F_(k r) whose image is t restricted to that neighbourhood. When T is empty, take the empty cover; when J is empty Step 3 forces T empty. Empty summands have already been omitted, and repeated nonempty summands are distinguished by the detector maps before their images in F are considered.

lean.statement:
theorem small_open_coproduct_cover {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (I : Type w)
    (Fi : I → Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u))
    (H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u))
    (j : ∀ i : I, Fi i ⟶ H) (hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j))
    (ι : ∀ i : I, Fi i ⟶ F) (q : H ⟶ F)
    (hfac : ∀ i : I, j i ≫ q = ι i) (hmono : ∀ i : I, Mono (ι i))
    (hopen : ∀ i : I, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith
      (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (ι i).hom)
    (hq : Epi q) (hcop : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace H) :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (k : J → I),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk H (fun r ↦ j (k r)))) ∧
      ∀ (T : Over S) (a : F.obj.obj (op T)),
        ∃ (𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.fppfPrecoverage T.left) (l : 𝒰.I₀ → J),
          ∀ r : 𝒰.I₀,
            F.obj.map (Over.homMk (𝒰.f r) rfl : Over.mk (𝒰.f r ≫ T.hom) ⟶ T).op a ∈
              Set.range ((ι (k (l r))).hom.app (op (Over.mk (𝒰.f r ≫ T.hom))))
